scope: Proposition 7.8 (The toric weight limits) of the manuscript “Exact Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer Formula from Low Selmer Corank” (preprints/Exact-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-Formula-from-Low-Selmer-Corank-October-7-2026/exact-bsd-low-selmer-corank.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 002 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 64b46603e174462e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 67. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: At every fixed stage i, the periods Pj,i(m) have coefficientwise limits as positive m tends to zero on the chosen p-adic branch and tends to infinity ordinarily. The limits, as group polynomials, have uniformly bounded coefficients as i varies. Up to a fixed nonzero scalar and group-like units, the limit of P0,i(m) is the stage image of the undepleted series b0 w. Consequently, when b0 w(z0) = 0, weights may be chosen at each stage with arbitrary prescribed additional precision so that P0,i(mi)(z0) −→ 0, sup i |P1,i(mi)(z0)|p < ∞.
